# The LuauG wire protocol, version 14

What a replica and an authority say to each other, byte for byte. This page is
generated from the schema the engine is compiled against (`api/wire/`), so it
describes exactly the protocol this tree speaks. ADR 0069 designed it, and
[ADR 0100](../decisions/0100-the-wire-protocol-is-published-and-versioned.md) is
the compatibility policy.

## Compatibility

- **One number, and an exact match.** A peer states the version it speaks first
  in `Hello`; an authority speaking another closes the connection. There is no
  negotiation and no partial compatibility.
- **The number changes whenever the bytes do** -- a field, a message, a layout, an
  encoding. An engine release that leaves the wire alone keeps the number, and
  the CHANGELOG says when a release moves it.
- **Numbers are permanent.** A field id, message id, channel or encoding value is
  never reused for anything else, in any version. A removed field is recorded as
  retired and stays claimed.
- The specification of a released version is this page at that release's tag.

## Transport

ENet, with 4 channels opened on every connection. Each message is one
packet and begins with a `u8` message type; nothing else frames it.

| Channel | Name | Delivery | What travels on it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Control | Reliable | Handshake, spawn, despawn, and the baseline acknowledgement. Everything whose loss cannot be recovered by the next tick's snapshot. |
| 1 | State | UnreliableSequenced | The per-tick diff. Unreliable because a dropped snapshot is superseded by the next one, and sequenced because an old one arriving late is worse than none. **This is the channel `flagsFor`'s missing `ENET_PACKET_FLAG_UNRELIABLE_FRAGMENT` would have broken**, silently, by putting a large snapshot on the reliable-fragmented path -- head-of-line blocking, which is exactly what the mode exists to avoid. |
| 2 | Intent | UnreliableSequenced | What a client did, never what happened. The client says it moved and fired; the authority decides whether it moved and whether it hit. |
| 3 | Ownership | UnreliableSequenced | Where an owner's parts are, from the owner (ADR 0099, protocol 14). Reserved as channel 3 since protocol 1 so its arrival shifted nothing. Unreliable and sequenced for the reason the State channel is: a lost state is superseded by the next tick's, and an old one arriving late would move a part backwards. |

## Primitives

- Integers are little-endian: `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, and `i32` in two's
  complement.
- `f32` and `f64` are IEEE-754, little-endian.
- `text` is a `u16` byte length and then that many bytes of UTF-8, with no
  terminator. A writer truncates at 65535 bytes.
- A reader that runs out of bytes rejects the whole message. Where a section says
  so, trailing bytes reject it too.

## Encodings

A field's value is one of these, fixed-width. `Encoding` is the value a schema
gives it.

| Encoding | Name | Bytes | Layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Bool | 1 | u8: 0 is false; anything else reads as true. |
| 1 | U8 | 1 | u8. |
| 2 | U16 | 2 | u16. |
| 3 | U32 | 4 | u32. |
| 4 | I32 | 4 | i32, two's complement. |
| 5 | F32 | 4 | IEEE-754 binary32. |
| 6 | F64 | 8 | IEEE-754 binary64. |
| 7 | Vector3 | 12 | f32 x, y, z. |
| 8 | Position | 24 | f64 x, y, z: a world coordinate. |
| 9 | CFrameD | 60 | f64 position x, y, z; then the rotation as nine f32, column by column: the right vector (x, y, z), the up vector, then the back vector. The look direction is the back vector negated. Nothing is quantised. |
| 10 | Color3 | 12 | f32 r, g, b, linear in [0, 1] by convention and not clamped. |
| 11 | NameAtom | 4 | u32: an interned string, numbered in the AUTHORITY's table. The `Snapshot` that carries it also carries the number's text, and 0 is no name. |
| 12 | InstanceRef | 4 | u32: a network id, 0 for none. |
| 13 | MaterialOverrides | 48 | u16 mask of the parameters set, two zero bytes, then eleven f32: colour r, g, b; transparency; emissive r, g, b; metalness; roughness; normal scale; alpha cutoff. Mask bit n is parameter n: Color 0, Transparency 1, ColorMap 2, NormalMap 3, MetallicRoughnessMap 4, Emissive 5, EmissiveMap 6, Metalness 7, Roughness 8, NormalScale 9, AlphaMode 10, AlphaCutoff 11, DoubleSided 12. |
| 14 | MaterialValues | 52 | The 48 bytes of `MaterialOverrides`, then u8 alpha mode, u8 double-sided, and two zero bytes. All zero when the part wears no runtime clone. |

## Identity

- **Network ids** are `u32`. 1 is the replicated root, the authority's
  `Workspace`. An instance is numbered from 2 upward as the authority first
  replicates it, and a number is never reused within a session.
- **A service** is never spawned. It travels under `0x7F000000` plus its index
  in the replicated classes below, and each end binds that to its own service of
  the same class. Its `Name` and `Parent` are ignored.
- **User ids** are `u32`: 1 is the player at a solo or hosting machine, and
  replicas are numbered 2 and up in the order they join.

## Handshake

1. The replica connects and sends `Hello`.
2. The authority checks the version, makes the player, and answers `Welcome`.
   A refusal is a disconnect.
3. Until `Welcome`, the authority ignores the replica's intents, owned state and
   remote calls.
4. From then on, every tick the authority sends, in this order: `Players` when
   the roster changed, `Despawn`, `Spawn`, `Ownership` when that changed, then
   `Snapshot`. The replica answers each snapshot it applies with `Ack`, and sends
   `Intent` and `OwnedState` every tick.

| Type | Name | Channel | Direction |

| 1 | [Hello](#hello) | Control | ToAuthority |
| 2 | [Welcome](#welcome) | Control | ToReplica |
| 3 | [Spawn](#spawn) | Control | ToReplica |
| 4 | [Despawn](#despawn) | Control | ToReplica |
| 5 | [Snapshot](#snapshot) | State | ToReplica |
| 6 | [Ack](#ack) | Control | ToAuthority |
| 7 | [Intent](#intent) | Intent | ToAuthority |

| 9 | [RemoteToAuthority](#remotetoauthority) | Control | ToAuthority |

### Hello

Type 1, on Control, ToAuthority. A replica announcing itself: protocol version, then the player token the authority gave it last time, or zeros the first time. **Version first, so a mismatch is refused before a single field is parsed** rather than after a decoder has already read a field id it does not have. The token is how a player who drops and comes back is the same player (ADR 0085).

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `1` |
| protocol | u32 | The protocol version the replica speaks. Any other than the authority's is refused. |
| tokenHigh | u64 | The player token the authority gave on an earlier join, or zero the first time. |
| tokenLow | u64 |  |

### Welcome

Type 2, on Control, ToReplica. Accepted: the peer's own `Player` id, the authority's tick, and the player token to send back on a reconnect -- the same id again (ADR 0085). A refusal is a disconnect with a keyed reason rather than a silence.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `2` |
| protocol | u32 | The authority's version; a replica refuses a Welcome in another. |
| userId | u32 | The replica's own player number, 2 and up. |
| tick | u64 | The authority's tick when it welcomed. |
| tokenHigh | u64 | The high half of the player token (ADR 0085). |
| tokenLow | u64 | The low half. |

### Spawn

Type 3, on Control, ToReplica. An instance entering interest: its network id and the class to create. Reliable, because an instance that is never created is a replica missing part of the world for good. **Its fields ride the snapshot**, as a whole record against a baseline that does not have it -- one decoding path for new and changed rather than two.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `3` |
| count | u32 |  |
| instances | count × | In ascending network id. A service is never spawned. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;className | text | Created by name; a class the replica does not have is skipped. |

### Despawn

Type 4, on Control, ToReplica. Instances a replica no longer has, in two lists: those the authority destroyed, then those that only left this peer's interest (protocol 6). **Leaving interest is the same event as a chunk being evicted**: one a script holds becomes a husk, reparented to nil, and is reported through the same `InstanceStreamedOut` a script already handles -- a second spelling of one thing would mean every game handles both.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `4` |
| destroyedCount | u32 |  |
| destroyed | destroyedCount × | Instances the authority destroyed. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 |  |
| streamedOutCount | u32 |  |
| streamedOut | streamedOutCount × | Instances that left this replica's interest and still exist on the authority. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 |  |

### Snapshot

Type 5, on State, ToReplica. The tick's diff against the peer's last acknowledged baseline, with a checksum over what was applied. **The checksum catches apply bugs and nothing else** -- interest gives a replica a strict subset of the world, so its hash is not the authority's and comparing them would be comparing two different worlds.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `5` |
| tick | u64 | The authority tick this is the world at. Older than one applied: dropped. |
| baseTick | u64 | The acknowledged tick this is a diff against, or 0: every record is then whole. |
| checksum | u64 | Over the replica's state once applied; see "The checksum". |
| intentTick | u64 | The newest of this replica's `Intent` ticks the authority has applied. |
| atomCount | u16 |  |
| atoms | atomCount × | Every name the records mention, in ascending number. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;atom | u32 | The authority's number for a name. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;text | text |  |
| recordCount | u32 |  |
| records | recordCount × | In ascending network id; an instance with nothing changed has none. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;schema | u8 | The class's index in "Replicated classes". |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;flags | u8 | Bit 0: a whole record, every field in order. Otherwise only what changed. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;fieldCount | u16 |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;fields | fieldCount × |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;wireId | u16 | See "Wire ids". |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;value | value | In the encoding of the field the wire id names. |

### Ack

Type 6, on Control, ToAuthority. Which baseline the replica now holds. Reliable, because a lost acknowledgement makes the authority diff against a baseline the replica has moved past.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `6` |
| tick | u64 | The snapshot tick the replica now holds, and may be diffed against. |

Type 7, on Intent, ToAuthority. One tick of a client's input, as actions rather than as results. The client says what it did; a client that could assert what happened is a client that always hits.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `7` |
| tick | u64 | The replica's tick. Not newer than the last one applied: dropped. |
| count | u16 |  |
| intents | count × |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;action | text | The input action's name. |

### Players

Type 8, on Control, ToReplica. Who is taking part: every player's number, their character's network id and their team's (protocol 14), zero for none, sent whole whenever any of it changes and once on welcome. Whole rather than as joins and leaves, because a roster is a few numbers and a list a replica can only ever replace cannot drift from the authority's.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `8` |
| count | u32 |  |
| players | count × | In join order. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;userId | u32 |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;character | u32 | The network id of their `Character`, or 0. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;team | u32 | The network id of their `Team`, or 0. |

### RemoteToAuthority

Type 9, on Control, ToAuthority. `RemoteEvent:FireServer` (protocol 7): the event's network id, a call number and a flags byte (protocol 8), the network ids of the instances the arguments name, and the arguments as the script module encoded them. A call number that is not zero is `RemoteFunction:InvokeServerAsync` asking, and names a `RemoteFunction`; zero names a `RemoteEvent`. The sender is the connection's player, never anything the message says.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `9` |
| remote | u32 | The network id of the `RemoteEvent` or `RemoteFunction`. |
| call | u32 | 0 for an event; otherwise the call a `RemoteFunction` answer belongs to. |
| flags | u8 | Bit 0: an answer. Bit 1: the answer is an error. Always 0 toward the authority. |
| refCount | u16 |  |
| refs | refCount × | The instances the arguments name, by position. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 | 0 for an instance the sender has no id for. |
| size | u32 | The byte length of what follows, at most 65552. |
| arguments | arguments | See "Arguments". |

### RemoteToReplica

Type 10, on Control, ToReplica. `RemoteEvent:FireClient` and `FireAllClients`, laid out as `RemoteToAuthority` is. On the Control channel, after the spawns of the same send, so an event created and fired in one tick is never named before it exists. With the reply flag set it is a `RemoteFunction`'s answer to the call number it carries, and with the failed flag the answer is the error the handler raised.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `10` |
| remote | u32 | The network id of the `RemoteEvent` or `RemoteFunction`. |
| call | u32 | 0 for an event; otherwise the call a `RemoteFunction` answer belongs to. |
| flags | u8 | Bit 0: an answer to `call`. Bit 1: the answer is an error, one string argument. |
| refCount | u16 |  |
| refs | refCount × | The instances the arguments name, by position. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 | 0 for an instance the sender has no id for. |
| size | u32 | The byte length of what follows, at most 65552. |
| arguments | arguments | See "Arguments". |

### Ownership

Type 11, on Control, ToReplica. The network ids of every part this replica owns (ADR 0099, protocol 14), sent whole whenever the list changes. Whole, as the roster is: a list the replica can only replace cannot drift from the authority's. Reliable and after the spawns, so it never names a part the replica has not been sent.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `11` |
| count | u32 |  |
| parts | count × | Every part this replica owns, in ascending network id. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 |  |

### OwnedState

Type 12, on Ownership, ToAuthority. One tick of the parts a replica owns: for each, its network id, its transform and its linear and angular velocity, as the owner's solver left them. The authority takes a state only for a part the sender owns at the moment it arrives, and moves the part there.

| Part | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| type | u8 | `12` |
| tick | u64 | The owner's tick. Not newer than the last one taken: dropped. |
| count | u16 |  |
| parts | count × |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;netId | u32 | A part the sender owns; any other is skipped. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cframe | CFrameD |  |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;linearVelocity | Vector3 | Metres per second. |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;angularVelocity | Vector3 | Radians per second. |

## Wire ids

A field in a `Snapshot` record is named by a `u16`:

- the common fields (below) by their own id;
- a field the class inherits from its base class by its id OR `0x4000`;
- a field of the class's own by its id OR `0x8000`.

A whole record carries every field in that order -- common, inherited, own --
each once.

## The checksum

FNV-1a, 64-bit (offset basis `0xCBF29CE484222325`, prime `0x100000001B3`), over
every instance the replica holds from this authority after applying, in ascending
network id: the id as 4 bytes, the class index as 1 byte, then for every field in
whole-record order its encoded bytes zero-padded to 64. Names are the
authority's numbers. A mismatch means the replica applied something wrongly; it
does not acknowledge that snapshot.

## Arguments

A remote call's arguments: a `u8` count, then each value as a `u8` tag and its
payload. 0 nil, 1 false, 2 true (no payload); 3 a number (`f64`); 4 a string
(`u32` length, bytes); 5 a vector (three `f32`); 6 an instance (`u32` index into
the message's refs); 7 a table (`u32` pair count, then key and value for each).
At most 64 KiB and eight tables deep. A key is never a vector, an instance or a
table, and a failed answer is exactly one string.

## Replicated classes

The class index is a record's `schema` byte.

### Common to every class

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Name | NameAtom | Scripts find things by name, so a replica whose names differ is a replica where `FindFirstChild` answers differently -- which is a divergence in the code rather than in the picture. |
| 2 | Parent | InstanceRef | **A network id, never a path.** A path is a string that goes stale the moment anything is renamed, and it is O(depth) to resolve on a replica that may not even hold the ancestors -- interest management gives it a subset by design. |

### 0 — BasePart

The moving half of nearly every game, and therefore the field set that decides whether replication is affordable at all. `Part` and `MeshPart` inherit it.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CFrame | CFrameD | Where the part is. **Read from the component and not through a property**, because `PhysicsSync` writes it there directly under a comment naming itself the QUIET write -- a schema that could only name properties could not replicate motion at all (ADR 0069). |
| 2 | Size | Vector3 | Rarely changes and is cheap to diff, but a part that resized on the authority and not on the replica is a collision mismatch a player experiences as being stopped by nothing. |
| 5 | Anchored | Bool | Decides whether the replica's own body is kinematic-driven or asleep, so a stale value costs a frame of the wrong physics. **In `rigidBodies` and not in `parts`**, which is where the schema first said it was: a part's simulation state is a separate component from its shape, because `scene` must not learn what a body is. |
| 6 | CanCollide | Bool | A door that opened on the authority and not on the replica is a player walking into a wall that is not there. |
| 7 | Material | NameAtom | The material asset the part wears, by URN, or none for the engine default. A name rather than the material itself: the file is content both machines have, as a mesh is. |
| 8 | MaterialParameters | MaterialOverrides | What the part overrides -- the tint and fade a game signals state with, which is gameplay rather than decoration. |
| 9 | MaterialClone | U32 | Which runtime copy of the material the part wears, by the authority's own number, or zero for the asset itself. Parts that share a copy share it on the replica too. |
| 10 | MaterialCloneValues | MaterialValues | What that copy changed. **Carried with each part that wears it** rather than as an object of its own, so a copy is never named before it has arrived; zero when the part wears none, so taking one off and putting it back is a change the diff sees. |
| 11 | MaterialCloneColorMap | NameAtom | A map the copy changed, by URN; the three below are the others. |
| 12 | MaterialCloneNormalMap | NameAtom | The copy's normal map, when it changed it. |
| 13 | MaterialCloneMetallicRoughnessMap | NameAtom | The copy's metallic-roughness map, when it changed it. |
| 14 | MaterialCloneEmissiveMap | NameAtom | The copy's emissive map, when it changed it. |

Retired, and claimed for ever:

- 3 `Color`, since 2.0.0: a part's colour is its material's parameter (ADR 0090); see MaterialParameters
- 4 `Transparency`, since 2.0.0: a part's see-through is its material's parameter (ADR 0090); see MaterialParameters

### 1 — CharacterBody

Carries `BasePart`'s fields too. A player's body, and the one class where the authority's answer and the client's guess are most visibly different. **Carries `BasePart`'s six too**, by `Extends` -- the first version of this entry said so in its doc and not in its data, and a replica would have held a character that never moved.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | VerticalVelocity | F32 | **Sent because a position alone cannot be interpolated**, and vertical because that is the axis a controller integrates itself: a `CharacterVirtual` is not a body the solver knows about, so gravity accumulates here. Two positions a tick apart say where a body was; this says where it is going, which is what lets a replica draw a smooth frame between two snapshots instead of stepping. |
| 2 | Grounded | Bool | Drives what a game shows -- a jump, a fall, a landing -- and is the authority's answer rather than something a replica can derive: whether a character is on the ground depends on collision the replica does not solve. |
| 3 | State | I32 | `Enum.CharacterState`, raw, exactly as the component stores it. It is what an animation picks a clip from, and a replica that guessed it from velocity would guess wrong at every transition -- which is where a player looks. |

### 2 — Model

Replicated for its scale alone: everything else about a model is its children, and they replicate as themselves.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scale | F32 | One number that moves every descendant, so sending it beats sending the descendants it moved. |

### 3 — Lighting

A service, under network id `0x7F000003`. Everything under it reaches every replica, whatever the distance. **The first service whose properties travel**: the time of day, the fog and the light. It is never spawned -- every world has one from boot, on both ends -- so it travels under a fixed id and a replica writes its own.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ClockTime | F32 | Night on the authority is night on every replica: the sun is where the game says it is. |
| 2 | GeographicLatitude | F32 | Where the sun's path runs, which with the clock is where every shadow falls. |
| 3 | Ambient | Color3 | The light in the shadows, which a game changes to say it is getting dark. |
| 4 | Brightness | F32 | How strong the sun is. |
| 5 | FogColor | Color3 | What the distance fades into. |
| 6 | FogStart | F32 | Where it starts to fade. |
| 7 | FogEnd | F32 | Where it is gone -- a storm rolling in is this number coming closer. |
| 8 | ExposureCompensation | F32 | A flash, a blinding moment, a cave entrance a game brightens. |
| 9 | EnvironmentDiffuseScale | F32 | How much the sky lights the world (ADR 0096). |
| 10 | EnvironmentSpecularScale | F32 | How much it is reflected. |
| 11 | ShadowSoftness | F32 | How soft the sun's shadows are. |
| 12 | GlobalShadows | Bool | Whether the sun casts at all. |
| 13 | AutoExposure | Bool | Whether the world's exposure follows the frame. |

### 4 — Decal

A scorch mark, a footprint, a poster (F2). Replicated since the snapshot's string table carries every name-shaped field rather than `Name` alone, which is what its image URN needed.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CFrame | CFrameD | Where the mark is -- relative to the part it is on, so a mark on a moving crate moves with it. |
| 2 | Size | Vector3 | How much of the world the mark covers. |
| 3 | Texture | NameAtom | The image, by content URN, through the snapshot's string table as every name travels. |
| 4 | Color | Color3 | What the image is multiplied by. |
| 5 | Transparency | F32 | A mark fading out is a game saying something. |

### 5 — ParticleEmitter

Sparks, smoke and magic (F2). Its particles are a picture and never travel -- each machine simulates its own -- but how an emitter is set up is what a game changes to say something, and a burst a script asked for on the authority has to happen on a replica too.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Enabled | Bool | A stream a replica keeps drawing after the authority stopped it is smoke from a fire somebody put out. |
| 2 | Rate | F32 | How dense the stream is, which a game changes to say how much is burning. |
| 3 | Lifetime | F32 | How far a stream reaches, with Speed. |
| 4 | Speed | F32 | How far a stream reaches, with Lifetime. |
| 5 | SpreadAngle | F32 | A jet and a fountain are one number apart. |
| 6 | Acceleration | Vector3 | Whether smoke rises or sparks fall. |
| 7 | Drag | F32 | How soon a puff stops. |
| 8 | Color | Color3 | What it looks like, which is the whole of what it is. |
| 9 | ColorEnd | Color3 | What it fades to. |
| 10 | Size | F32 | How big a particle is born. |
| 11 | SizeEnd | F32 | How big it dies. |
| 12 | Transparency | F32 | How solid it is born. |
| 13 | TransparencyEnd | F32 | How solid it dies. |
| 14 | LightEmission | F32 | Whether it glows or blends. |
| 15 | Brightness | F32 | How hard it glows. |
| 16 | Shape | I32 | What one particle looks like. |
| 17 | Emitted | U32 | **How bursts reach a replica**: a running total of what `Emit` asked for, so a replica spawns the difference it has not seen -- the low 32 bits, because a difference is all it ever takes, and it wraps safely. |

### 6 — Folder

**Replicated with no fields of its own, and that is the point.** A folder is structure: a `Parent` reference to one has to resolve on the replica, so the folder has to be there. Its `Name` and `Parent` come from the common set.

### 7 — RemoteEvent

Replicated so a message has something both ends agree it is for (ADR 0077): its network id is the address a `RemoteToAuthority` or `RemoteToReplica` names. No fields of its own; a message is not state.

### 8 — ReplicatedStorage

A service, under network id `0x7F000008`. Everything under it reaches every replica, whatever the distance. A service with no fields whose contents travel (ADR 0080): every instance under it reaches every replica, whatever its position, parented to the replica's own `ReplicatedStorage`.

### 9 — RemoteFunction

Replicated for the reason `RemoteEvent` is (ADR 0079): a question and its answer both name it. Its handler is a function on the authority and never travels.

### 10 — Part2D

The 2D layer's moving half (ADR 0088, protocol 11): where a sprite is, how it is turned and which frame of its sheet it shows. A replica drives it kinematically, as it drives a `BasePart`.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Position | Vector3 | Where it is, on the plane. **A `Vector2` travels as a `Vector3` with a zero z** (ADR 0088): twelve bytes the codec already has, rather than an encoding of its own for four fewer. |
| 2 | Rotation | F32 | Degrees, as authored. A turned crate on the authority is a turned crate everywhere. |
| 3 | Size | Vector3 | The picture's size and the collider's, for the reason a `BasePart`'s travels. |
| 4 | Velocity | Vector3 | Sent because a script on the replica reads it -- a run animation picks its frame from it -- and because it is what a later version extrapolates with. |
| 5 | AngularVelocity | F32 | The same argument as `Velocity`. |
| 6 | Color | Color3 | Games say things with colour; the same argument as a `BasePart`'s. |
| 7 | Transparency | F32 | A blinking hurt sprite is a gameplay fact. |
| 8 | Anchored | Bool | Decides whether the replica's body is kinematic-driven or ground. |
| 9 | CanCollide | Bool | A door that opened on the authority must be open on the replica. |
| 10 | Sensor | Bool | Whether it pushes: a replica's own character must pass through a coin. |
| 11 | Shape | I32 | `Enum.Shape2D`, raw: what it is drawn and collides as. |
| 12 | ZIndex | I32 | Which sprite is in front; a game changes it to say something. |
| 13 | FlipX | Bool | **The facing of a sprite is animation state**, and a replica that did not receive it would show every other player running backwards half the time. |
| 14 | FlipY | Bool | The same as `FlipX`. |
| 15 | Image | NameAtom | The picture, by URN, through the snapshot's string table as a `Decal`'s is. |
| 16 | ImageRectOffset | Vector3 | **The frame of a sprite sheet**: a walk cycle is this changing, so it is the other half of a replicated sprite's animation. A `Vector2` as a `Vector3`, as `Position` is. |
| 17 | ImageRectSize | Vector3 | The frame's size, beside its offset. |
| 18 | Filter | I32 | `Enum.TextureFilter`, raw: pixel art stays crisp on every screen. |

| 3 | Size | F32 | How far it reaches. |

### 18 — TeamService

A service, under network id `0x7F000012`. Everything under it reaches every replica, whatever the distance. Where the sides live (ADR 0099, protocol 14): every `Team` under it reaches every replica, whatever its distance, as `ReplicatedStorage`'s contents do.

### 19 — Team

A side (ADR 0099, protocol 14). Who is on it is not a field of the team: it is the roster's third column, beside each player's character.

| Id | Field | Encoding | Why it travels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Color | Color3 | What a side looks like on every machine: a name tag painted on one replica and not another is two games. |
| 2 | AutoAssign | Bool | Only the authority assigns, but a replica's scripts may show which sides are open. |

## Not replicated

Every other concrete class is deliberately off the wire, and this is why.

| Class | Reason |
|---|---|
| Terrain | Its bulk is not a property and a field is megabytes. A world's ground arrives with the world -- from the scene, or later from a streamed cell -- and a sculpt is rare, authored, and not a per-tick fact. ADR 0069 decides this by name so the next person does not have to work out whether it was considered. |
| Player | Lives under `NetworkService`, which is not replicated, and each end makes its own: an authority one per peer, a replica one for itself and one for each player the `Players` roster names. What a replica knows of a player -- their number, their character and their team -- is the roster, not a snapshot of the instance. |
| DataModel | The root. Every world has exactly one and it is created at boot on both sides, so there is nothing to spawn and nothing to reference by id. |
| Attachment | A joint frame. The replica's bodies are kinematic-driven from the authority's transforms and solve nothing, so the frames that produced those transforms are work it would do twice and disagree about. |
| Bone | The same argument as `Attachment`, plus one: a bone's world transform is derived from an animated pose, and the pose is derived from state that does replicate. |
| Weld | A welded part's transform is resolved from its anchor every tick. The authority sends the resolved transform; sending the weld as well would give the replica two answers. |
| WeldConstraint | The same as `Weld`. |
| BallSocketConstraint | The replica does not solve constraints -- its bodies are kinematic. What it needs is where the limbs ended up, which is `BasePart.CFrame`. |
| HingeConstraint | The same as `BallSocketConstraint`. |
| FixedConstraint | The same as `BallSocketConstraint`. |
| Ragdoll | A ragdoll is parts and constraints, and the parts replicate. The ragdoll instance is the recipe rather than the result. |
| Camera | A replica's view is its own. Replicating it would take the camera away from the player, which is the one thing a client must decide. |
| Script | Source code is not world state. A replica runs the game it was shipped, and a server that could push source to a client would be a server that can run code on it. |
| ModuleScript | The same as `Script`. |
| Sound | Playback position is local and drifts by design. What replicates is the world event that starts a sound, not the sound. |
| AudioGroup | A mixer bus. What a player hears at what volume is theirs. |
| PointLight | Lighting is drawn from world state a replica already has. A light that moved because its parent moved needs no message of its own. |
| SpotLight | The same as `PointLight`. |
| PostEffect | Abstract. Its five classes are replicated by name. |
| Material | A material is an asset reference, and assets arrive with the build rather than over the wire. |
| InputAction | Input is the client's to send as intent and never the authority's to push back. ADR 0041 already routes it through one dispatch; replicating it would give a server a second way to press a player's keys. |
| InputBinding | A rebinding is a preference on one machine. The same as `InputAction`. |
| InputContext | Which bindings are live is local UI state. The same as `InputAction`. |
| ScreenGui | Screen-space UI is drawn from local state by local scripts. What a player sees on their own HUD is not a fact the authority owns. |
| BillboardGui | World-space UI is built by each peer's own scripts, as the screen's is: everything under it is a UI class the wire does not carry, so sending the root alone would send an empty board. A name tag over another player's character is made on each client from what IS replicated -- the character and its name. |
| SurfaceGui | World-space UI. The same as `BillboardGui`. |
| Tilemap2D | Its bulk is its painted cells, which are not a property, as a `Terrain`'s field is not (ADR 0069, decision 7; ADR 0088): a level arrives with the world -- from the scene, or from a script that builds it the same way on both ends -- and a live edit would be a message of its own, which no game has asked for yet. |
| NavigationArea | What it says is a question only the authority's navigation asks (ADR 0098): a path is searched where the game's scripts run, and a replica that wants one asks with a remote. The part it labels is replicated; the label is not something a replica draws. |
| NavigationLink | A way across for the authority's paths. The same as `NavigationArea`. |
| NavigationAgent | It walks its part on the authority's tick, and the part's `CFrame` is what arrives -- interpolated like any other part's. Sending the agent too would send a second account of one motion. |
| Frame | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| TextLabel | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| TextButton | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| TextInput | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| ImageLabel | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| ImageButton | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| ScrollFrame | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| UICorner | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| UIListLayout | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| UIPadding | Screen-space UI. The same as `ScreenGui`. |
| AnimationPlayer | **The first candidate for protocol 2, and out of N1 on purpose.** What an animation needs is which clip, at what time, at what weight -- three fields whose meaning is a blend tree the wire would have to describe. N1 replicates where bodies are, which is what a player sees; making the limbs move the same way needs a design of its own and would double this milestone. |
